facts: The State is before us aggrieved by and dissatisfied with a judgment of acquittal passed by a Division Bench of the High Court of Himachal Pradesh, Shimla in Criminal Appeal No. 41 of 1994.

Sarwan Singh (since deceased), Jagtar Singh (since deceased) as well as Nazar Singh and Baldev Singh, respondents herein were prosecuted for commission of an offence under Section 302 read with Section 34 and Section 323 read with Section 34 of the Indian Penal Code (for short, 'the Code') for causing death of one Lamber Singh and simple hurt to one Avtar Singh.
The occurrence took place at about 9.30 p.m. on 30.03.1993 in the field of the deceased Lamber Singh.
Lamber Singh had gone to tie his dog therein.

PW-1 Bakshish Singh, brother of the deceased, after some time heard him shouting whereupon he ran towards the field and found that Sarwan Singh armed with gandasi and others armed with lathis had been assaulting the deceased.
issues: Whether the accused persons formed a common intention to cause death of the deceased Lamber Singh.
Whether the evidence of PW-2, an injured witness, should be relied upon.
Whether the High Court was correct in disbelieving the evidence of PW-1 and PW-2.
petitioner_arguments: Respondents having gone to the field of the deceased variously armed must be held to have formed a common intention to cause death of the deceased Lamber Singh.
PW-2 being an injured witness, the High Court should not have disbelieved his evidence particularly when implicit reliance thereupon had been placed by the learned Trial Judge.
There was furthermore no reason as to why the evidence of PW-1 also could not have been relied upon.
respondent_arguments: The impugned judgment is correct and the accused persons did not form a common intention to cause death of the deceased Lamber Singh.
court_reasoning: It appears that the deceased went to his field on hearing the barking of his dog at 9.30 p.m.
There is nothing to show that all the accused persons were waiting for him or had come to assault him with any common intention.
According to the prosecution, a dispute arose with regard to laying down of a pipeline three months prior to the date of occurrence.
It, however, appears that the matter was settled through the intervention of the panchayat.
holding: The appeal preferred by the State is allowed and the judgment of acquittal passed by the High Court is set aside.
